difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a point x of an algebraic space X over S, the existence of a locally finite type representative Spec(k) -> X of x is equivalent to the existence of a scheme U with an etale morphism U -> X and a closed point u of U mapping to x (source lines 5020-5030). The forward direction is a computation: Spec(kappa(u)) -> U is of finite type and U -> X is representable and locally of finite type, so the composite is locally of finite type. The reverse direction takes a surjective etale U -> X and uses that U x_X Spec(k) -> U is locally of finite type, picks a finite type point v of U x_X Spec(k), shows its image u in U is a finite type point, and shrinks U so that u becomes closed.
